issues.description: Predicate inverts the layer exception but lacks a stated invariant comment
issues.detail: The new clause `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` encodes a real rule from the CSS cascade spec: only statement-form `@layer name;` is allowed before `@import`; block-form `@layer name {}` is a style rule and triggers the cascade, disqualifying later imports. That invariant should be a one-line comment above the clause so the next reader does not have to reconstruct it from PostCSS internals.

issues.description: Prefer a named predicate over `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'`
issues.detail: `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` is a PostCSS-shape test masquerading as domain logic. A small helper like `isStatementAtRule(node)` (or `node.nodes === undefined`) reads as the concept being tested and survives future PostCSS node-shape changes better. The behavior is correct; the literacy is missing.

issues.description: Test coverage misses the legitimate statement-form `@layer foo;` before `@import`
issues.detail: The added accept case would lock in the asymmetry: `@layer foo, bar;` (statement) before `@import` must remain valid, while `@layer foo {}` (block) must reject. Only the reject case is added. A paired accept-case test pins the invariant from both sides and prevents a future regression that over-tightens the rule.

review.summary: The fix is algorithmically correct and minimal: it distinguishes statement-form `@layer name;` (allowed before `@import` per the cascade spec) from block-form `@layer name {}` (a style rule that disqualifies later imports) by checking `node.nodes === undefined`. The change is RIGOROUS in behavior but NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT — the spec invariant is not stated in the code, and the PostCSS-shape check would read better as a named predicate. The test suite adds the reject case but not the symmetric accept case for statement-form layers, leaving one side of the invariant unpinned.
